title: `_sanitize_next_path` does not reject a backslash, so `/login?next=/\evil.com` is a working post-authentication open redirect on the real domain
claimUnderTest: frontend/middleware.js:52-54 — "server.py::_sanitize_next_path rejects absolute URLs and CR/LF on the way back out." The guard is presented as the complete sanitiser for the post-login destination.
observed: The guard rejects `http://`, `https://`, a leading `//`, a non-`/` prefix and CR/LF — but not a backslash. `next=/\evil.com` survives verbatim and is returned as `{"ok":true,"redirect":"/\\evil.com"}`. `frontend/app/login/page.jsx:25` re-checks only `next.startsWith("/")`, which `/\evil.com` satisfies, then line 50 calls `router.push(data.redirect)`. Next resolves the href with the WHATWG URL parser, which normalises `\` to `/` for special schemes, so `new URL('/\\evil.com', location.href)` is `http://evil.com/`. Driven end to end in Chromium against the real login form, the browser issued a top-level navigation to `http://evil.com/` immediately after a successful login. `/\/evil.com` passes too.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W22/open-redirect-repro.py   # needs a backend on :8001 with ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1; header-only check: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"x","password":"y","next":"/\\evil.com"}'
reproduction.expected: redirect coerced to "/" exactly as it is for `//evil.com` and `https://evil.com`
reproduction.actual: redirect = "/\\evil.com"; Chromium then requests http://evil.com/ — captured as offsite requests: ['http://evil.com/']

userImpact: A link on the genuine chaseupside.com domain — `https://chaseupside.com/login?next=/\attacker.tld` — shows the real login page, takes the operator's real password, and then drops the browser on the attacker's site. That is the standard credential-phishing amplifier: the victim has no domain cue that anything is wrong, and the attacker's landing page can render a convincing "session expired, sign in again" form. With a single shared operator credential (W22-F003) and no MFA, one success is full compromise.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding in the 531-item index mentions open redirect or _sanitize_next_path.

whatWorks: The three cases the guard was written for — `//host`, `http(s)://host`, and CR/LF header injection — are all correctly coerced to "/". The frontend's own `startsWith("/")` check is a second layer and also correct as far as it goes.
rootCause: A denylist of four dangerous prefixes instead of an allowlist. The set of strings a browser treats as scheme-relative is larger than `//`: RFC 3986 says backslash is not a path separator, but the WHATWG URL Standard (which every browser and Next's router use) maps `\` to `/` inside special-scheme URLs.
requiredRepair: Replace the prefix denylist with a parse-and-compare: `u = urlsplit(value)`; reject unless `u.scheme == '' and u.netloc == '' and value.startswith('/')`, after normalising backslashes to forward slashes first. Add `/\\evil.com`, `/\/evil.com`, `/%5Cevil.com` and `/\t/evil.com` to whatever test pins this.
dependencies: None. Self-contained one-function fix in server.py.

title: The rate limiter keys on an unvalidated client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For`, so every public endpoint's limit is bypassed by rotating one header
claimUnderTest: src/api/rate_limit.py:9-11 — "60 requests/minute per IP … 1000 requests/hour per IP (burst cap)", and server.py:2840-2842 "Also applies rate limiting to public endpoints … to protect against scraper abuse."
observed: `_client_ip_from_request` returns the FIRST comma-separated entry of `X-Forwarded-For` whenever the header is present, with no trusted-proxy check and no fallback preference for `request.client.host`. nginx sets `X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, which APPENDS `$remote_addr` to whatever the client sent — so in production the first entry is entirely attacker-controlled. Measured on a second backend booted without `RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS`: the real client IP was driven to a hard 429, and 20 consecutive requests sent from that same socket with rotating `X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.N` all returned 200.

reproduction.command:
# boot a backend on :8001 without RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS, then:
for i in $(seq 1 70); do curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health; done
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health   # 429
for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%s ' -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.$i" http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/health; done
reproduction.expected: 429 for all 20, because they originate from the throttled socket

numericProof.formula: 429_count over 20 spoofed-XFF requests issued from an already-throttled socket

userImpact: The scraper-abuse defence the module exists for does not exist. Anyone can pull the 2.08 MB `/api/public/league` contract, or the 47 KB `/api/news` feed, at whatever rate the box will serve — and, because `/api/auth/login` sits behind the same limiter, the login endpoint has no effective throttle either (W22-F003).

priorFinding.note: No prior finding mentions X-Forwarded-For or the rate limiter.

whatWorks: The token-bucket arithmetic itself is correct and thread-safe: 60 requests pass and the 61st gets 429 with a sane `Retry-After`, refill is proportional to elapsed time, and the `_MAX_TRACKED_IPS` eviction bounds memory. The limiter fails open around a raising `should_rate_limit`, which is the right posture. Nothing here is wrong except the key.
rootCause: `_client_ip_from_request` trusts a hop-by-hop header unconditionally. The comment "First entry in the chain is the original client" is true only when every hop appends and the leftmost hop is itself trusted — which is exactly what `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` does NOT guarantee for a directly-reachable client.
requiredRepair: Prefer `X-Real-IP` (nginx sets it from `$remote_addr` and OVERWRITES, so it is not client-controlled) and fall back to `request.client.host`; use `X-Forwarded-For` only after stripping a configured count of trusted proxy hops from the RIGHT. `_MAX_TRACKED_IPS`-based eviction also becomes a memory-exhaustion lever while the key is attacker-chosen.
dependencies: nginx already sets `X-Real-IP $remote_addr` in both `location /api/` and `location /`, so no deploy change is needed.

title: Login has no throttle of its own, no lockout and no failure backoff — 200 wrong-password attempts landed at 223 req/s with zero 429
claimUnderTest: HANDOFF.md's known-issues list states there is NO login rate limiting. The code's own position is the opposite: `/api/auth/login` is in `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT`, so the 60/min public-endpoint limiter does cover it.
observed: Both are half right, and the net effect is HANDOFF.md's. The generic limiter is the ONLY throttle: `auth_login` itself has no attempt counter, no per-account lockout, no backoff, and no delay. That limiter is (a) shared with every other public endpoint — 60 requests to `/api/public/league` in the same minute leave the operator locked out of their own login — and (b) keyed on a spoofable header (W22-F002). Measured on a limiter-live backend: 120 wrong-password POSTs from one IP → {401: 18, 429: 102}; the same 200 POSTs with a rotating `X-Forwarded-For` → {401: 200} in 0.9 s, zero 429. There is exactly ONE credential (`JASON_LOGIN_USERNAME`/`JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD`) and no second factor. Guest-pass tokens are 24 random URL-safe bytes and are not brute-forceable, but the operator password is whatever a human chose.

reproduction.command:
# on a backend booted WITHOUT RATE_LIMIT_BYPASS_IPS:
.venv/bin/python - <<'EOF'
import json,time,urllib.request,urllib.error
c={}
t=time.time()
for i in range(200):
    b=json.dumps({"username":"jasonleetucker","password":f"wrong-{i}"}).encode()
    r=urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:8001/api/auth/login",data=b,headers={"Content-Type":"application/json","X-Forwarded-For":f"198.51.100.{i%250}"})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(r,timeout=10) as x: s=x.status
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: s=e.code
    c[s]=c.get(s,0)+1
print(c, time.time()-t)
EOF
reproduction.expected: a lockout or exponential backoff after a handful of failures for the same username
reproduction.actual: {401: 200} in 0.9 s = 223 attempts/second, no 429, no delay, no lockout

numericProof.formula: attempts/sec = attempts / elapsed; 401-only means every attempt was evaluated

userImpact: An 8-character lowercase-alphanumeric operator password is ~2.8e12 candidates; at 223/s from one host that is not reachable, but the rate is bounded only by the attacker's willingness to run parallel sources, and nothing anywhere records or alerts on a burst of failures. More practically: a leaked or reused password gets confirmed instantly, and there is no signal in any log, on `/api/status`, or in the alert path that a credential-stuffing run happened at all.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A10-F08 cites 'the login rate-limit gap' as one of the HANDOFF.md items that IS still true. Confirmed in substance and refined: a generic limiter does cover the route, it is simply shared and bypassable, and the missing pieces are the login-specific ones (lockout, backoff, failure telemetry).

whatWorks: `hmac.compare_digest` is used for the two cron bearer tokens. Guest-pass validation is a hashed-token table lookup, so it is constant-time by construction and the plaintext is never stored. The cookie is HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite=Lax with a 30-day max-age matching the server-side TTL, session ids are `uuid.uuid4().hex` (122 bits from os.urandom), and guest sessions carry a server-side `expires_at_epoch` re-checked on every request so a stretched cookie cannot outlive its pass.
rootCause: Login was treated as just another public endpoint. Nothing distinguishes 'one anonymous read of a public board' from 'one attempt at the only credential that exists'.
requiredRepair: Add a per-username failure counter with exponential backoff (and a hard lockout window), keyed independently of IP so header spoofing cannot reset it; emit a log line and an alert on N failures; and fix the limiter key (W22-F002) so the IP-side throttle is real. `password == JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD` at server.py:9838 should also become `hmac.compare_digest` for consistency with the bearer paths.
dependencies: W22-F002 — the IP-side half is worthless until the key is trustworthy.

title: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1` silently makes `changeme` a full admin password, has no production guard, and is invisible on every health/status surface
claimUnderTest: tests/conftest.py:11 — "production rejects ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1 by design." server.py:174-176 — "this guard prevents a misconfigured restart from silently shipping a known password."
observed: Neither is true. There is no production check of any kind: the branch is `if not password: if _env_bool('ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV', False): password = 'changeme'`. Nothing consults an environment name, a hostname, `JASON_AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE`, or anything else. The only signal is one WARNING at import time, which scrolls out of `journalctl` and appears nowhere at runtime — `startup_validation.run_all()` checks eight things and none of them is the login password or this flag, so `/api/health.startupChecks` reports `total: 8, ok: 8, failed: 0` on a box running the placeholder password. Proven live: on a backend with `ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1` and `JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD` unset, `jasonleetucker`/`changeme` returned 200, `/api/auth/status` reported `isAdmin: true`, and `GET /api/admin/guest-passes` returned 200. The second failure mode is separate and not guarded at all: `.env.example` ships `JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD=changeme`, so an operator who copies it to `.env` gets the same outcome with the flag OFF, because the import-time guard fires only on UNSET, never on weak.

reproduction.command: cd /home/user/riskittogetthebrisket && env -u JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV=1 .venv/bin/python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');import server;from fastapi.testclient import TestClient;c=TestClient(server.app);print(c.post('/api/auth/login',json={'username':'jasonleetucker','password':'changeme'}).status_code);print(c.get('/api/auth/status').json())"
reproduction.expected: either a refusal to boot in a production-shaped environment, or at minimum a visible degraded marker on /api/health and /api/status

numericProof.formula: count of startup_validation checks whose name matches JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD|ALLOW_DEFAULT_LOGIN_DEV

userImpact: One stray line in `.env` — or one `.env.example` copied verbatim — hands full admin over `chaseupside.com` to anyone who guesses a five-year-old default, and the operator has no way to notice: the app looks healthy on every surface they can check. Combined with the unbounded login rate (W22-F003), detection time is the only thing standing between the misconfiguration and compromise.

priorFinding.note: The April 2026 report (audit/AUDIT_REPORT_2026-04-28.md C1) closed the hardcoded-default incident; nothing in the 531-item prior index re-examines the escape hatch it introduced.

whatWorks: The import-time RuntimeError for the fully-unset case is real and correct — `EnvironmentFile=-.../.env` means a missing .env produces a crash loop rather than a silent weak-password boot, which is the right failure. The password is genuinely out of source: 0 tracked files carry a literal, and the three docs that quoted the old one now carry `«REDACTED — see audit/AUDIT_REPORT_2026-04-28.md C1»`.
rootCause: A dev escape hatch with no environment discriminator, plus a startup validator that checks directories and SQLite files but no security-relevant configuration.
requiredRepair: (1) Gate the flag on an explicit non-production marker (e.g. refuse when `JASON_AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE` is true, or require an `APP_ENV=dev`). (2) Add two `startup_validation` checks — `env:JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD` required, and a `fatal=False` check that fails when the effective password equals the placeholder — so the condition is visible on `/api/health`. (3) Change `.env.example` to `JASON_LOGIN_PASSWORD=` (empty) so a verbatim copy crash-loops instead of booting weak. (4) Fix the false comment at tests/conftest.py:11.
dependencies: Note that adding the check to startup_validation puts it on TWO anonymous endpoints — see W22-F005; emit the check name only, never the value.

title: `/api/status`, `/api/health` and `/api/scaffold/status` hand absolute deploy paths, env-var presence, feature-flag state, the full source inventory and live session counts to anonymous callers
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md's endpoint table for `/api/leagues`: "stable `key` → `displayName` + roster settings; **no Sleeper IDs leaked**", and the routing section's "no endpoint exposes raw Sleeper IDs to the UI".
observed: `/api/leagues` honours the invariant exactly — 808 bytes, zero Sleeper ids. `/api/status`, on the same public allowlist and with no comment justifying its presence there, emits `leagues[].sleeperLeagueId` for BOTH registry leagues. It also emits, anonymously: absolute deploy paths (`/home/user/riskittogetthebrisket/data/dynasty_data_2026-08-04.json`, `.../data/rank_history.jsonl`), the complete `featureFlags` map with `gateStatus`, `served_source_coverage` naming all 21 ranking sources with per-source row counts, `source_health.source_failures` with free-text failure reasons, `run_events`, and payload byte sizes. `/api/health` adds the `startupChecks` array — three absolute directory paths, two SQLite filenames, the league-registry keys, and `env:PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES → "missing (optional)"`, which tells a stranger the allowlist env var is unset and therefore that the admin username is the in-code default `jasonleetucker` — plus `session_cookies` naming the three paid subscription session files, per-breaker `lastError` strings, `memberInMemorySessions: 42`, `sessions.persistedCount`, and `backup_health.newestBackupPath`. `/api/scaffold/status` adds two more absolute paths and identity-pipeline counts.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/status | grep -o '"sleeperLeagueId": "[0-9]*"'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health | grep -o 'env:PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES.\{0,60\}'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/status | grep -o '/home/[^"]*'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/leagues | grep -c sleeperLeagueId
reproduction.expected: the /api/leagues invariant applied consistently across the public allowlist; no absolute paths, no env-var inventory, no operator counts
reproduction.actual: /api/status: 2 sleeperLeagueId values + 2 absolute paths + 15 feature flags + 21 source names; /api/health: env:PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES 'missing (optional)' + 3 absolute dirs + 3 vendor session filenames + 42 in-memory sessions; /api/scaffold/status: 2 absolute paths; /api/leagues: 0

numericProof.formula: count of _PUBLIC_API_EXACT routes emitting host filesystem paths or registry Sleeper ids

userImpact: An attacker profiling the deployment gets the app root, the data directory layout, which SQLite files exist, which env vars are unset (so which defaults are live — including the admin username), which feature flags are on, the entire scraping source list with coverage, and the live session count, without authenticating. None of it is exploitable on its own; all of it shortens the reconnaissance step for everything else in this shard. The `/api/leagues` redaction is undone in substance by a sibling on the same allowlist, so the documented invariant does not describe the system.

priorFinding.note: CONFIRMED for the mechanism and both named routes, refuted on the stated impact of the id leak. PRIOR-A23-F16 says the ids enable 'direct enumeration of rosters, transactions and drafts via Sleeper's open API'. That is true, but the incremental exposure is ZERO: config/leagues/registry.json is a TRACKED file in a PUBLIC repository carrying both ids, and SECURITY.md explicitly accepts that ('the league configuration … readable by anyone'). I verified the ids do unlock the second league via api.sleeper.app. The real defect is that the invariant CLAUDE.md documents is applied to one public route and not another — a doc/code contradiction, not a data leak. The absolute-path half is confirmed unqualified, and I add the env-var-inventory, feature-flag, source-inventory, vendor-session-filename and session-count disclosures the prior finding did not cover.

whatWorks: `/api/leagues` genuinely withholds every Sleeper id while still serving the roster settings the frontend needs, and `/api/metrics` and `/api/uptime` carry nothing sensitive. The global exception handler never returns a traceback — it emits `errorType` only and logs the trace server-side — and 13 anonymous probes with traversal, null-byte, negative and overflow inputs produced zero raw exception text.
rootCause: `_PUBLIC_API_EXACT` was assembled per-consumer ('the /league page needs this') without a payload review. Every other public route in the set carries an explaining comment; `/api/status`, `/api/health`, `/api/metrics` and `/api/scaffold/status` carry none.
requiredRepair: Either move `/api/status` and `/api/scaffold/status` behind the session gate (the only in-tree consumer of `/api/status` is `/admin`, which is already a private page — this is what makes PRIOR-A06-F08 possible) or give them an anonymous projection: drop `leagues[].sleeperLeagueId`, replace absolute paths with basenames, drop `startupChecks` env rows and `run_events`, and keep the full payload for authenticated callers.
dependencies: `/admin` currently relies on `/api/status` being public for its load-time fetch (W22-F008); gating it is the fix for both.

title: `sitemap.js` is an unwired fourth consumer of the public/private page split and advertises the private `/trades`; `robots.js` still allows the `/league/insider-trading` exception it was supposed to close
claimUnderTest: public-routes.js:5-8 — "One predicate, three consumers: middleware.js, AppShellWrapper.jsx, robots.js … It lives here, pure and dependency-free, because those three used to disagree." And :44-62 — the `/league/insider-trading` exception, added because "`robots.txt` serves `Allow: /league/`, so that spinner is on an indexable URL."
observed: There are FOUR consumers. `frontend/app/sitemap.js` imports nothing from `public-routes.js` and hardcodes its own "Static public routes" list containing `"/trades"` — the one route whose privacy the module's own header comment spends a paragraph explaining. The live `sitemap.xml` therefore publishes `https://chaseupside.com/trades` while middleware 307s that exact path to `/login` and `robots.txt` disallows it. Separately, the `/league/insider-trading` fix was applied to `isPublicPath` only: `robots.js` spreads `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` and ignores `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS`, so the emitted `robots.txt` is `Allow: /league/` + `Disallow: /` with no `Disallow: /league/insider-trading`. Under longest-match precedence that URL remains crawlable-by-policy — which is the precise condition the comment says the exception was written to end. (`robots.js` also omits `PUBLIC_EXACT`, so the legitimately-public `/draft-capital` shim is disallowed.)

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/sitemap.xml | grep -o '<loc>[^<]*trades</loc>'; curl -s -o /dev/null -D- http://127.0.0.1:3000/trades | grep -i '^location'; curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/robots.txt; grep -n 'public-routes' frontend/app/sitemap.js || echo 'sitemap.js: NO IMPORT'
reproduction.expected: every sitemap entry satisfies isPublicPath(); robots.txt disallows every PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS path
reproduction.actual: <loc>https://chaseupside.com/trades</loc> while /trades → 307 /login?next=%2Ftrades; robots.txt has Allow: /league/ and no insider-trading Disallow; sitemap.js: NO IMPORT

numericProof.formula: count of sitemap <loc> paths for which isPublicPath(path) === false

userImpact: No data leaks — every private page still 307s and robots.txt still disallows `/trades`. What breaks is the guarantee: the module that exists to stop these three files disagreeing is not consulted by the fourth, so the next private page added to `sitemap.js`'s static list, or the next `/league/*` page added anywhere, repeats the `/league/insider-trading` incident with nothing to catch it. A crawler that reads the sitemap and ignores robots gets a permanent 307 loop on an advertised URL.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers sitemap.js or robots.js consistency.

whatWorks: The gate itself is airtight in both directions: all 18 private pages probed anonymously returned 307 to `/login?next=<encoded original>`, the four public ones returned 200, `/draft-capital` returned a real 308 to its new home, and neither anonymous 200's HTML contained any private-board token. `robots.js` correctly rebuilt itself as an allowlist, and `middleware.js` is genuinely the single page-auth gate now that server.py registers no page routes (confirmed: `curl :8000/rankings` → JSON 404).
rootCause: `sitemap.js` predates or was written alongside `public-routes.js` and was never migrated; `robots.js` was migrated to `PUBLIC_PREFIXES` before `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS` existed and was not revisited when the exception landed.
requiredRepair: Import `isPublicPath` in `sitemap.js` and filter every entry through it (fails closed for future pages); spread `PUBLIC_EXACT` into `robots.js`'s allow list and `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS` into a `disallow` array; add a test that asserts every sitemap entry satisfies `isPublicPath` and every `PRIVATE_EXCEPTIONS` entry appears in robots' disallow.

title: Operator-grade actions and pages are gated on session PRESENCE, not on the admin allowlist, so a guest-pass holder can trigger a production scrape, an email send and an intel crawl
claimUnderTest: server.py:9856-9859 — a guest-pass session's username is left as the literal `"guest"` so "downstream admin gates … reject guests automatically — a guest can browse the private surface but cannot trigger admin actions or generate more passes." And frontend/app/admin/page.jsx:7-9 — "Access is gated server-side by PRIVATE_APP_ALLOWED_USERNAMES."
observed: True only for the six routes under `/api/admin/*`, all of which I confirmed return 403 `admin_required` to a non-admin session. The operator-grade actions that live OUTSIDE that prefix have no allowlist check at all — the session-presence middleware is their entire authorization. `POST /api/scrape` (`async def trigger_scrape`) never calls `_require_admin_session`; `POST /api/test-alert` is declared `async def test_alert()` with no `Request` parameter, so it cannot check anything; `POST /api/intel/refresh` accepts any session (`if not is_cron and not session: 401`) and applies only a per-user cooldown. Page-side, `middleware.js` checks cookie PRESENCE only, so `/admin` and all three `/tools/*` returned 200 to the non-admin `e2e-test-user` session, and `/admin`'s sole load-time fetch is `/api/status` — a PUBLIC route — so its "Not authorized" branch is unreachable. Separately, every guest-pass session is created with username `"guest"` while `user_kv.user_state` has `username TEXT PRIMARY KEY`, so all guests share one row: watchlist, `activeLeagueKey`, `selectedTeam`, `siteWeights`, dismissed signals and `customAlerts` are overwritten guest-by-guest, and a guest's `customAlerts` rules are executed by the daily sweep.

reproduction.command: SECRET=$(cat .../e2e_secret.txt); curl -s -c /tmp/c -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/test/create-session -H "Authorization: Bearer $SECRET"; for p in /admin /tools/source-health /tools/ros-data-health /tools/trade-coverage; do curl -s -b /tmp/c -o /dev/null -w "$p %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3000$p; done; grep -n 'async def trigger_scrape' -A3 server.py; grep -n 'async def test_alert' -A2 server.py
reproduction.expected: 403 admin_required for operator-grade actions and pages, matching the /api/admin/* posture the docstrings describe
reproduction.actual: /admin 200, /tools/source-health 200, /tools/ros-data-health 200, /tools/trade-coverage 200; trigger_scrape and test_alert contain no admin check (test_alert takes no Request at all)

numericProof.formula: count of operator-grade handlers outside /api/admin/* that call _require_admin_session

userImpact: Anyone the operator hands a guest pass to — the stated purpose is showing the tool to leaguemates — can start a full production scrape (minutes of Playwright work plus outbound traffic to every ranking site), fire the configured email alert, kick off the multi-minute budgeted Sleeper intel crawl, and read the operator dashboard including live feature-flag state and scrape internals. They can also silently overwrite every other guest's saved settings and plant alert rules that the nightly sweep will run. None of it is destructive to player data, but none of it is what the docstring promises either.

priorFinding.note: CONFIRMED at runtime — /admin returns 200 to a non-admin session and its only mount-time fetch is the public /api/status, exactly as described. Extended on three axes the prior finding did not cover: the three /tools/* pages behave identically, three operator-grade API routes outside /api/admin/* have no allowlist check at all, and every guest-pass session collides on the single user_kv row keyed 'guest'.

whatWorks: `_require_admin_session` is correct and is the first statement of all six `/api/admin/*` handlers — five verified live returning 403 to a non-admin session and 401 anonymously. Guest passes are well built: 24-byte `secrets.token_urlsafe` tokens, SHA-256 at rest with the plaintext shown once, a 30-day creation cap, revocation, opportunistic purge, and a server-side `expires_at_epoch` re-checked on every request so a stretched cookie cannot outlive the pass. The two cron bearer routes fail closed — they short-circuit before touching cookies when the token is unset, use `hmac.compare_digest`, and require `auth_method == "password"` on the session fallback, which excludes guest and e2e sessions.
rootCause: Two authorization tiers exist (session, allowlist) but only the `/api/admin/*` prefix was wired to the second one. Route placement, not route capability, decided which tier applied.
requiredRepair: Add `_require_admin_session` to `trigger_scrape`, `test_alert` (which needs a `Request` parameter first) and `post_intel_refresh`'s non-cron branch; give `middleware.js` an admin-page list checked against a lightweight allowlist claim, or have `/admin` and `/tools/*` fetch a genuinely admin-gated endpoint on mount so the existing "Not authorized" branch can fire; and namespace guest user_kv rows per pass id (`guest:{guest_pass_id}`) instead of the shared literal.
dependencies: The `/admin` page fix is coupled to W22-F005 — gating `/api/status` makes the page's existing 403 branch work with no page change.

title: The public-league payload's name-based blocklist cannot see derived values: 393 anonymous trade grades encode bracketed value ratios computed from `rankDerivedValue`
claimUnderTest: src/api/public_activity_valuation.py:1-12 — "The public src/public_league package is strictly isolated from private rankings … The raw values that drive the grade never leave the backend — only the derived grade block appears on the public payload." SECURITY.md — "player valuations, trade tooling, waiver and draft analysis, and BDVM output are all login-gated."
observed: The literal claim holds: `assert_public_payload_safe` walks every dict key at every depth against a 39-name blocklist and I confirmed 0 hits for any blocklisted field across ten anonymous public endpoints totalling 2.6 MB. But the guard is a NAME blocklist, so it is structurally blind to a value derived from a blocked field and stored under an unblocked name. `/api/public/league` serves 191 graded trades / 393 graded sides anonymously. Each side carries its full received and sent asset lists AND a grade letter that is a five-band quantisation of `package_value(received)/package_value(sent)` at cut points 3/8/15/25/40 percent, where the values come from the private contract's `displayValue`/`rankDerivedValue`. That is 393 published inequality constraints over a few hundred distinct assets — a solvable system for relative board values to within-band precision, obtainable with no session.

reproduction.command: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/public/league | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);f=d['sections']['activity']['feed'];g=[s for t in f for s in (t.get('sides') or []) if isinstance(s,dict) and s.get('grade')];print(len(f),'trades',len(g),'graded sides');print(collections.Counter(s['grade']['grade'] for s in g))"
reproduction.expected: per the isolation docstring, nothing on the anonymous payload that is a function of rankDerivedValue
reproduction.actual: 191 trades / 393 graded sides; Counter({'A+': 114, 'F': 60, 'A': 55, 'D': 53, 'B+': 41, 'B': 25, 'A-': 23, 'C': 22}), each paired with the exact asset list on both sides

numericProof.formula: published constraints = graded sides; each is log2(5) ≈ 2.32 bits about package_value(received)/package_value(sent)

userImpact: A competitor who wants the board does not need to break the auth gate; they need to fit 393 published ratio brackets. The recovered board would be coarse — bands, not values — but ordering and rough magnitude are exactly what the tool sells. Second-order: every manager's per-trade verdict from the operator's private model is public and attributed by `ownerId` and `displayName`, which is league-social information the operator may not have intended to publish.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding examines the derived-value channel through the public contract guard.

whatWorks: The isolation architecture is real and does the hard part correctly: `src/public_league` never imports the contract, `server.py` injects a callable, and the raw numbers genuinely never appear — verified byte-level across ten endpoints. The `/api/draft-capital` redaction is the same problem solved properly: `_redact_draft_capital_for_public` strips all five rookie-board fields from 72/72 picks for anonymous callers, stamps `rookieBoardRedacted: true`, and does it on a COPY so the shared TTL cache is not poisoned for the authenticated /draft page. That is the pattern the grade channel needs.
rootCause: `assert_public_payload_safe` was designed against accidental field passthrough (a rename, a new bundle key) and is well suited to that. Deliberate derivation is a different threat and the guard has no way to express it, because the derived output is legitimately named `grade`.
requiredRepair: This is a product decision, not a bug fix, and it should be recorded as one rather than left implicit in a docstring that reads as an absolute. If the grades stay: state in the isolation docstring and in SECURITY.md that a bounded derived signal is deliberately published, and consider widening the bands or dropping the letter to a three-way win/fair/loss to cut the recoverable precision. If they should not be public: pass `activity_valuation=None` on the anonymous path and keep grades for authenticated callers only, mirroring `_redact_draft_capital_for_public`.
dependencies: None technically; needs an owner decision on intent.

title: `/api/draft-capital` serves auth-varying bodies under `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60` with no `Vary: Cookie`, and `/api/auth/status` sends no cache directive at all
claimUnderTest: deploy/nginx/chaseupside-proxy.conf:88-95 — "tests/api/test_cache_control_privacy.py documents the invariant that auth-gated endpoints must not meet a shared cache … /api responses pass through uncached with their app-stamped private/no-store Cache-Control intact."
observed: The shared-cache half of the invariant holds — nginx attaches `proxy_cache` only to `/_next/static/`, and `private` would bar a shared cache anyway. The per-browser half is unhandled. `/api/draft-capital` returns two different bodies for the same URL depending on the session cookie (the five rookie-board fields plus `rookieBoardRedacted`), yet stamps `Cache-Control: private, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` and `Vary: Accept-Encoding` only. A browser that loaded the public `/league` draft-capital tab and then signed in serves the redacted body from its private cache for up to 60 s (300 s stale-while-revalidate), so `/draft` renders with no rookie names; the reverse holds after logout. `/api/auth/status` returns username, `authMethod` and `isAdmin` with NO `Cache-Control` header at all, so its freshness is left to browser heuristics — the only session-identity endpoint in the app without `no-store`, while `/api/user/state` and `/api/leagues` both set it.

reproduction.command: for u in /api/draft-capital /api/auth/status /api/user/state; do echo "-- $u"; curl -s -o /dev/null -D- -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000$u" | grep -iE '^(cache-control|vary):' | tr -d '\r'; done
reproduction.expected: draft-capital: Vary: Cookie alongside private (or no-store); auth-status: Cache-Control: no-store
reproduction.actual: draft-capital: 'cache-control: private, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300' + 'vary: Accept-Encoding' (no Cookie); auth-status: no cache-control header emitted at all

numericProof.formula: seconds a stale variant can be served after an auth transition = max-age + stale-while-revalidate

userImpact: For up to six minutes after signing in on a browser that had just viewed the public league page, `/draft` shows a rookie board with every name, position and value blank and no explanation. Confined to one browser profile, so this is a correctness and confusion defect rather than a disclosure one. The missing `no-store` on `/api/auth/status` risks a stale identity — showing a signed-out shell to a signed-in user or vice versa — after a back-navigation.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers Vary on the redacted draft-capital response.

whatWorks: The redaction itself is exemplary and I could not break it: full payload cached, redaction applied per-response on a copy, `rookieBoardRedacted` stamped so a client can tell redaction from absence. Every genuinely private route carries `private` or `no-store`; nginx caches only `/_next/static/`; and no `/api/*` response I saw set both `Set-Cookie` and a cacheable directive.
rootCause: The response was designed as a single cacheable artifact and the redaction was added later as a per-response transform. The cache directive was not revisited to declare the new dimension of variance.
requiredRepair: Add `Vary: Cookie` to both `JSONResponse` returns in `get_draft_capital` (or set `no-store` on the authenticated variant and keep `private, max-age=60` for the anonymous one, which is the cheaper option since the anonymous variant is what the high-traffic public page hits). Add `Cache-Control: no-store` to `auth_status`. Extend `tests/api/test_cache_control_privacy.py` to assert that any route whose body varies by session declares it.
